Subject: SLA pricing — modular credits and escalation seats

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the product demo last week — Meridian liked the latency profile and the fallback model idea. Procurement asked me to get a concrete pricing construct for SLA and premium support: specifically we want to understand (1) modular uptime-credit bundles (how credits scale with volume), (2) escalation-seat pricing (for a named on-call escalation engineer and 24/7 coverage), and (3) any pilot / short-term trial pricing for the first 6 months.

To be clear on our expected consumption: ~50M tokens/month initially, with bursts up to 2x for launches. We care most about response windows for Sev-1 and Sev-2 (30m/4h targets) and an uptime credit schedule tied to monthly availability.

Can you sketch an initial structure we can share with Procurement? If you have a simple matrix or an anchored example, that would help move things quickly.

Best,

Subject: Re: SLA pricing — modular credits and escalation seats

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and the numbers.

High level proposal (sketch):
- Modular uptime-credit bundles: 3 tiers (Bronze / Silver / Gold) priced as a percent of monthly usage spend: Bronze = 0.5% credit per 99.5–99.8% availability band, Silver = 1.5% credit per 99.2–99.5% band, Gold = 3% credit for <99.2%. We can structure as pre-purchased credit blocks sized to your commit (e.g., blocks of $5k / $20k / $50k) that scale with volume.
- Escalation-seat pricing: Named escalation seat = flat monthly fee. Options: Standard seat ($6k/mo) for daytime + business-hours triage, Premium 24/7 seat ($18k/mo) with direct on-call escalation and N2 routing. We also offer fractional seat pricing if you only want handoff during launches.
- Pilot pricing (6 months): we can offer a reduced pilot uplift where SLA credits are capped and seat fees discounted by 50% for the first 6 months; pilot renews into normal pricing or a mutually agreed commit.

I've attached a one-page pricing matrix (redwood-pricing_matrix-v2.xlsx) that maps usage bands to credit block sizes and shows example math for your 50M tokens/month profile. A few asks from us to firm numbers:
1) Expected commit (tokens or $) for year 1 to size blocks.
2) Whether you need true 24/7 named contact or prefer on-call rotation sharing.
3) Any regulatory requirements that would mandate Private deployment / dedicated capacity.

If useful, Markus can send a counter-anchor with a blended commit discount (I cc'd him). Also included a short term note on fallbacks/canary — credits don't apply if we trigger automatic fallback to compatible model variants, we'll log the decision.

Next steps: review the attached matrix and tell us which anchor (Bronze/Silver/Gold) you want us to price for a draft Statement of Work.

Regards,

Emma — quick follow-up from engineering / product pricing perspective. Two practical tweaks that help alignment with ops: 

1) Anchoring offer: instead of static % credits per band we can offer a blended "commit ladder" where the credit % steps down as commit grows (e.g., 3% credits on first $50k, 1.5% on next $150k, 0.5% thereafter). This gives Meridian predictable unit economics as you scale.

2) Escalation-seat add-on: define an "on-call attach" hour bucket. If you expect heavy launch support (e.g., 72-hour intensive window), charge additional attach-hours at a reduced hourly rate vs. full premium seat. This avoids full monthly premium seat commitment for short windows.

I've attached a short note (sla-escalation-seat-terms.pdf) that lists seat definitions and handoff SLAs. Laura, happy to review the doc together on Thursday if Emma is available.

Best,
Markus Klein

Laura / Markus — thanks for the outline. Procurement has two immediate asks / constraints: 

1) We need a floor anchor for discounts tied to a 12-month commit — can you show a version with (a) no commit, (b) 12-month $250k commit, (c) 12-month $750k commit. We want to see effective % credit and effective per-token price at each commit.
2) For the pilot: request a 6-month pilot at 60% of published seat pricing (not 50%) and a cap on total credits applied during the pilot to $20k. We'll entertain a conversion bonus to encourage us to convert.

Additionally, please clarify if credits are applied as invoice offsets or as future service credits. We prefer invoice offsets but will accept service-credit accounting if there is a firm convert-to-invoice clause.

Can you return a short comparison table and an SOW-lite that we can circulate with legal?

Regards,
